title: On-Demand Attention: Language Models Know When to Recall
summary: ODA replaces full-attention decoding, where every generated token reads the entire KV history, with local-first decoding that invokes global attention only when a lightweight recall head predicts it will help. The cost is training a recall head per model, maintaining the full KV cache in memory (so no memory savings), and adopting a modified vLLM build with GPU-side conditional execution. It can fail when the recall head mispredicts the benefit of global reads on out-of-distribution workloads, silently degrading quality while the speedup depends on context length being long enough for skipped reads to dominate.
rationale: The method fits a single-GPU setup since pretrained weights stay frozen and only a small head is trained, but the gain is workload- and context-length-dependent and requires custom serving code, so it warrants validation on the reader's own long-context traffic before production adoption.
technique: Selective global attention via learned recall head

claims.statement: ODA replaces full-attention decoding, where every generated token reads the entire KV history, with local-first decoding that invokes global attention only when a lightweight recall head predicts it will help. The cost is training a recall head per model, maintaining the full KV cache in memory (so no memory savings), and adopting a modified vLLM build with GPU-side conditional execution. It can fail when the recall head mispredicts the benefit of global reads on out-of-distribution workloads, silently degrading quality while the speedup depends on context length being long enough for skipped reads to dominate.

Recovers most of the performance lost under local attention while substantially reducing global reads, with practical decoding speedups over full attention at long context lengths; no specific factor reported in the abstract.
